hypothesis: A sparse high-energy virtual spectrum in the coarse radial basis can make an energy-ceiling scan falsely look converged; compare energy and angular tails together with an independently refined radial reference.
fixed_physics: Z70 empirical Fermi nucleus; closed 68-electron [Xe]4f14 core; all 19 core radial orbitals; five external normalized core-orthogonal DF spinors; both antisymmetrized second-order diagrams and scalar DF-connected Dyson roots; Dirac-Coulomb only.
exact_subset_replays: For coarse: l<=4/6/7/8 and emax=5/20/50/100/200Ha. For fine: l<=4/6 and emax=5/20/50/100/200Ha. Every subset retains all bound virtuals and re-solves all five Dyson roots; no coupling threshold.
factor_controls: l6->l8 at the same coarse metric and energy ceiling; 50->100->200Ha at each common radial/angular model; ns123->230 at common l6 and ceiling. Fine reference orbitals and all five baseline attachment energies come from the independently converged fine V68 reference, never spliced with coarse states.
root_branch: For each declared subset use [epsilon_DF-0.1,epsilon_DF] if Sigma(epsilon_DF)<0, otherwise [epsilon_DF,epsilon_DF+0.1]; reject any intervening nonzero-weight pole or absent root. No experimental root selection.
limits: Two radial grids and finite l/energy ceilings are convergence controls, not an extrapolated tail bound or a proof of higher-order, off-diagonal, Breit/QED or radiative-operator accuracy.
stopping: Finish the two complete five-state captures and all declared matched controls, or stop a failed numerical gate with preserved failure evidence; do not silently reduce physical space or extend caps. New long-run caps are increased relative to the previous 1000-second five-state coarse run because actual virtual-pair count and radial contraction cost increase.
